subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Must every browser-origin Admin HTTP RPC request, including explicit `none` and trusted-proxy deployments, pass `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` before body parsing and method dispatch?
rationale: The current documentation implies a uniform browser-origin boundary, but explicit no-auth and proxy-auth deployments have different trust assumptions; only the security owners can confirm whether any exception is intentional.

options.title: Enforce One Origin Boundary
options.body: Apply the shared browser-origin allowlist before all Admin HTTP RPC authentication and dispatch paths, with regression tests for every supported auth mode.

options.title: Permit Explicit No-Auth Exposure
options.body: Treat `auth.mode: none` as an intentional origin-check exception and document the resulting browser threat model and required private-ingress controls.

recommendation.title: Enforce One Origin Boundary
recommendation.body: Apply the shared browser-origin allowlist before all Admin HTTP RPC authentication and dispatch paths, with regression tests for every supported auth mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue timeline routes the security escalation to this person, while the implementation history is shared across the admin plugin and Gateway origin code.
